title: The Last Table
tagline: One closing shift. A hundred fresh starts.
description: On the last night of a neighbourhood diner, a meticulous cook and an eternally late regular try to reunite the people who made it home. Their plan involves a borrowed karaoke machine, a very long table and absolutely no reservations.
conversation: A warm ensemble comedy about neighbours and small acts of kindness. The humour comes from clashing personalities, rather than embarrassment or cruelty.
contentNotes: Mild arguments; no horror or graphic violence.

title: Blue Hour Radio
description: A quiet overnight radio host finds a box of unsent voice messages. Over one rain-soaked week, she invites strangers to finish the conversations they left behind.
conversation: Intimate and reflective, with a focus on listening and friendship. Mandarin dialogue has English subtitles. A good choice for a quieter evening.
contentNotes: Themes of grief and separation; no graphic imagery.

title: A Borrowed Sun
tagline: A little light goes a long way.
description: In a town that keeps its daylight in jars, an apprentice lamplighter accidentally lends the last sunbeam to a travelling cloud. She sets out with a paper fox to bring morning home.
conversation: Playful original animation with a gentle adventure and a hopeful tone. The shortest film in the programme, suited to families who enjoy imaginative worlds.
contentNotes: A brief storm sequence and mild peril.

title: Platform Zero
tagline: The last train has an extra stop.
description: A station announcer notices a train that appears on no timetable. When its passengers begin asking about tomorrow, she has until sunrise to decide which arrival to announce.
conversation: A contained, dialogue-driven mystery with mounting tension. Suspense rather than horror; there are no supernatural jump scares. Keep the explanation of the train secret.
contentNotes: Threatening situations and loud train sounds; no graphic violence.

title: Sideways Summer
tagline: The wrong turn was the right idea.
description: Two cousins borrow a delivery van for a beach trip, only to discover its final parcel still needs delivering. A wrong address turns their free afternoon into a wonderfully inconvenient island tour.
conversation: An upbeat road comedy centred on a bickering friendship. More energetic than The Last Table, with sunny locations and a loose, spontaneous rhythm.
contentNotes: Mild language and comic driving mishaps.

title: Small Orbits
tagline: Distance is a matter of perspective.
description: A caretaker on a tiny orbital garden receives a seed addressed to someone who never existed. Growing it brings a surprising visitor and a reason to stop counting the days until home.
conversation: Thoughtful science fiction about belonging, with an imaginative setting and a warm central relationship. A contemplative adventure rather than an action spectacle.
contentNotes: Isolation and a brief equipment emergency.

title: The Paper City
tagline: Every street has a story to unfold.
description: A young mapmaker discovers that her grandfather's folded maps open into miniature cities. When one begins to disappear, she must follow an unfinished route and learn why he stopped drawing.
conversation: A family adventure built around curiosity, craft and intergenerational friendship. Brisker and more puzzle-led than A Borrowed Sun.
contentNotes: Mild fantasy danger; themes of ageing.

title: After the Rain Stops
tagline: Some things take their own time.
description: A retired gardener and a novice architect inherit the same flooded courtyard. Through a season of small repairs, they argue over what to preserve and discover what each is ready to change.
conversation: An unhurried character drama about patience and renewal. Malay dialogue has English subtitles. The longest film in this programme; allow time to settle into it.
